findings.finding: F1. R4 describes a mechanism sjawhar/legion#2538 does not have, and #2538 deletes the behaviour R1 specifies. #2538 writes a legion.dev/pod-shape JSON annotation (podShapeRecord{Image,Resources,Volumes,Mounts,Disk}) rather than storing the template; podShapeDrift falls back to image alone when the annotation is absent; relaunch's decision becomes (!installing && !roundCovers(l.kind) && len(r.shapeDrift(s, l.kind)) > 0) and roundCovers excludes only the controller's pod, so after #2538 a launch never replaces an issue pod for drift.
findings.answer: Decision D5 and task T9. The plan is written for branch A (#2538 not in this branch's base, its state today: gh pr view 2538 -> OPEN, mergedAt null) and spells branch B fully: the account joins the round's compared settings by reading s.Spec.PodTemplate.Spec.ServiceAccountName directly, outside the annotation, since every Sandbox stored before #2538 carries none and those are exactly the pods INFRA-321 must move; and the account term also sits in relaunch's decision outside !installing, which is what keeps R1's install exemption for the controller's pod, the one kind no round covers. The branch is decided by an observation (gh pr view 2538 --json state,mergedAt, plus whether the tree carries drift.go) recorded in the implement handoff.

findings.finding: F1 (continued). Nothing fails loudly if #2538 merges after this issue's tester has run: #2538 rewrites relaunch's replace expression wholesale and touches relaunch_test.go, one_container_test.go, shared_pod_test.go, busy_test.go and watch_test.go, so an account term added to today's expression can disappear in the merge; R4's remedy is a comment to a human, which nothing checks.
findings.answer: Decision D5 makes the guard structural: the launch-side account tests live in a new file, packages/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox/account_drift_test.go, never inside relaunch_test.go. A merge that drops the account term then fails that test in the merge-queue build. The comment on #2538 (T9 branch A) names that file as the guard.

findings.finding: F2. R1's 'keeps its Sandbox and disk' is false for an issue pod: podkind.go:138-142 and manifest.go:484 make an issue pod's disk a generic ephemeral volume created and deleted with the pod. Only the controller's claim and a cache's volume survive.
findings.answer: Recorded as spec departure S1. The plan builds what R1 asks behaviourally ('as for image drift'): the Sandbox is kept, the pod replaced, and an issue pod's disk goes with it exactly as it does for image drift today. No acceptance line changes. The cost is written where the docs already list what ends an issue pod's disk, docs/kubernetes.md:3761-3762, as part of task T8.

findings.finding: F3. Ambiguity over the compared surface (the live pod in R1/R2, the stored template in R4) and over an empty serviceAccountName: the daemon writes "" into the template when service_account is unset while the API server stores default on the pod, so comparing raw values would read every pod of such a deployment as drifted.
findings.answer: Decision D1: R1 and R2 compare the live pod's spec.serviceAccountName (the API server does not rewrite that field, unlike the reservations Autopilot rewrites, which is why templateResized reads the template); branch B of T9 compares the stored template's own serviceAccountName; and "" is read as default on both sides, so neither a raw "" from an unset configuration nor an omitempty-dropped template value can be read as drift.

findings.finding: F4. Every site that fills ${MODEL_TOKEN_AUDIENCE} today breaks once the fixtures carry a second placeholder, and R5 names only three of them: config/kubernetes_test.go:1456 and :1547, runtime/sandbox/operatorpod_test.go:23, stage4a's key-file arm (a plain cp, no substitution at all), claude-backend-sandbox.sh's substitution inside its gateway arm, stage4b's shape_problems jq, stage4b-pods.test.ts's Run, deploy/kubernetes/operator-route/README.md and scripts/e2e/README.md. script-functions.test.ts also fails on any stage-script helper nothing calls.
findings.answer: Tasks T6 and T7 list every site, each with its file and line, including deploy/kubernetes/operator-route/README.md (an operator-facing document, not a proof fixture) and both model routes of each script. The new helper is a lib script with its own caller in each of the three scripts, so script-functions.test.ts's rule is satisfied by wiring rather than by addition.

findings.finding: F5. A2's git grep cannot pass as R5 is written (scripts/e2e/README.md:1203's 'ServiceAccount `legion-worker`' matches the backtick alternative, and R5 asks only that the README name the variable), and the expression misses deployment-pod-block-verdict.test.ts:203's bare legion-worker.
findings.answer: Task T7.8 changes README:1203 to name the variable, so A2's grep passes as the spec wrote it; T7.7 changes :203 as well, so the gap the expression cannot see is closed anyway. The plan records both the six sites the grep returns today and the one it misses, so a later reader cannot mistake a green grep for a clean tree.

findings.finding: F6. R5's 'before any kubectl call' is unsettled (the audience gate it would mirror sits inside a gateway-only case in two of the three scripts), its LEGION_E2E_POD_FILE carve-out contradicts the sentence it qualifies, and A2's wording does not check the ordering at all: a script that creates a namespace and then refuses would pass it.
findings.answer: Decision D4: the variable is required unconditionally in all three scripts, outside every model-route arm and before the first cluster call (stage4a:210-211 before :277, stage4b:3129 before :3195, claude-backend-sandbox.sh:1098 before :1235), matching stage4b's existing unconditional audience gate; the parenthetical is implemented as what shape_problems compares against in the LEGION_E2E_POD_FILE path (the block's own account). The acceptance table adds the check A2's wording lacks: each script run with the variable unset under a PATH whose first kubectl records its argv and exits 1, asserting the refusal and that the recorder file does not exist.

findings.finding: F7. A3's 'grep -n -i account docs/kubernetes.md' returns 60 lines before any change and decides nothing; R6's 'an account counterpart in its log line' has two readings, one of which breaks watch_test.go:361's prefix count and the other its 'one warning per Sandbox'; warnImageDrift's name is quoted at docs/kubernetes.md:1613; and ReconcileOrphans skips cache Sandboxes before it warns.
findings.answer: Decision D2 and tasks T3 and T8. The image line stays byte-identical and a second line is added, so the existing count holds; the function is renamed warnPodDrift and docs/kubernetes.md:1613 is updated in the same commit; cache Sandboxes stay unwarned for the account as for the image, which the comment states. The acceptance table keeps A3's grep as the spec names it and adds the decisive form: grep -n 'ServiceAccount' docs/kubernetes.md read at :1605-1621, :2876 and :3761-3762, plus a unit test of the exact warning line.

findings.finding: F8. A1's conditional clause ('if #2538 is merged, its round treats a changed account as changed') cannot be read as a verdict: a test that does not exist is indistinguishable from a test that was dropped.
findings.answer: Task T9 names the branch-deciding command and, for each branch, the test that must exist: branch A, account_drift_test.go in a file of its own plus the comment on #2538; branch B, a test that a changed account is drift both for a template carrying the pod-shape annotation and for one carrying none. The implement handoff records the observation and the branch taken.

findings.finding: F9. Smaller things: no production code reads a pod's live service account today, so R1/R2 introduce the first such read; cacheSandboxShape does not inspect the account, so a cache on the old account falls to R2 rather than to the boot census; deployment-pod-block-verdict.jq:82 skips an unset account, a second convention beside R3; two comments become wrong (relaunch.go:60-63, one_container_test.go:339); deploy/kubernetes/daemon/legion.yaml.example:161 and docs/kubernetes.md:1874 still name legion-worker; ci.yaml already has the fixture in a path filter.
findings.answer: Decision D7 brings the jq onto R3's rule with its own tests (a clear defect in a file this change edits, fixed here rather than deferred); decision D6 records why the two example files keep legion-worker (examples of an operator's own value, read by config_example_test.go, outside A2's paths, and one of Legion's own allowed names); task T1.3 updates both stale comments; the plan states the cacheSandboxShape and census facts so no later round re-checks them, and that CI needs no new wiring.

specDepartures.spec: R1: at a launch into a live issue or controller pod whose spec.serviceAccountName differs, relaunch 'replaces the pod and keeps its Sandbox and disk, as for image drift'.
specDepartures.plan: The Sandbox is kept and the pod replaced; an issue pod's disk is not kept, and goes with the pod exactly as it goes for image drift today. The controller's claim and a repository cache's volume do survive, so R2's wording holds. The plan writes that cost into docs/kubernetes.md's list of what ends an issue pod's disk.
specDepartures.evidence: packages/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox/podkind.go:138-142 gives an issue pod a generic ephemeral volume whose claim the kubelet creates with the pod and deletes with it; manifest.go:484 states the same; podkind.go:412-420 and repocache.go:116 are the two claims that outlive their pods.

specDepartures.spec: R6: docs/kubernetes.md names account drift where it lists what replaces a pod (pinning section, repository-cache section).
specDepartures.plan: Three sections are edited, not two: the pinning section (:1605-1621), the repository cache (:2876) and the third list of launch-replacement reasons, 'What ends an issue pod's disk' (:3761-3762), which would otherwise be left stating that an image, a moved stream, an enrollment, a session-database key, a role_config_files mount, a launcher Secret or the old disk shape are the only reasons.
specDepartures.evidence: docs/kubernetes.md:3761-3762 reads 'a launch replaces the pod, because it cannot run the launching role as a pod created now would: another image, a moved worker stream, a secrets-broker enrollment, session-database key or role_config_files mount the pod lacks, a role's launcher Secret that no longer binds it, or a Sandbox of the disk shape before this release'.
